questions.q: For a support agent searching a single box for a customer's name or phone, then needing their open cases, which pattern fits best?
options: A single TYPEOF query against Case
SOSL first to find matching contacts/accounts, then a SOQL semi-join to pull their open cases
A GROUP BY query against Contact
An anti-join against Account
questions.explain: This is the SOSL-then-SOQL pattern: free-text search finds the person/company, then a targeted SOQL query pulls the specific related records needed.

questions.q: Can a SOQL aggregate function directly calculate 'average time a case stayed open' from CreatedDate and ClosedDate alone?
options: Yes, using the DATEDIFF() aggregate function
Yes, using AVG(ClosedDate - CreatedDate) directly
Yes, but only with GROUP BY and no WHERE clause
No — SOQL aggregates summarize existing field values, they don't calculate elapsed time between two dates on their own
questions.explain: SOQL's aggregate functions summarize values already present in fields; computing elapsed time between two dates needs a stored duration/formula field, not a built-in aggregate.

questions.q: SELECT TYPEOF What WHEN Account THEN Name WHEN Case THEN CaseNumber ELSE Id END FROM Task is used for what kind of question?
options: Listing logged activities related to different object types, with different fields depending on which type
Finding every Task regardless of its related object
A semi-join between Task and Case
An aggregate count of Tasks grouped by Status
questions.explain: TYPEOF is exactly the tool for returning different fields depending on what a polymorphic field (like Task's What) actually resolves to.

questions.q: To find open, high-priority cases for a specific account by name, which SOQL feature from earlier lessons is used?
options: SOSL's RETURNING clause
A parent-to-child subquery nested inside Account
Child-to-parent dot notation (Account.Name) combined with WHERE filters
A TYPEOF clause
questions.explain: Filtering Case rows by a condition on the related Account's Name field is a straightforward child-to-parent dot-notation query, not a subquery or TYPEOF.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of the SOSL-then-SOQL pattern over trying to do an entire support search in one SOQL query?
options: It uses fewer total characters of code
SOSL can search free text across multiple object types at once to find who matches, before SOQL retrieves exactly the related fields needed
It avoids governor limits entirely
SOQL cannot be used after a SOSL search in the same transaction
questions.explain: SOSL is suited to the broad, free-text 'who matches' question across several objects, while SOQL is suited to the precise, structured follow-up — splitting the work matches each language's strength.
